why: Cities are nodes and 'differ in exactly one character' is an unweighted edge, so the minimum number of hops is a BFS shortest path, the same shape as Word Ladder.
hints: Draw the cities as dots and connect two when they differ in one letter. What are you being asked to find in that picture?
Shortest path in an unweighted graph is BFS. Instead of comparing every pair, generate neighbours: for each of the 3 positions try all 26 letters and check membership in a set of cities.
Set of cities, queue of (city, dist), visited set. Each city generates 75 candidates, so O(75 n). Return -1 if endCity is never reached.
pitfalls: A hop may only land on a city in the list; generated strings not in the set are not allowed.
Comparing all pairs is O(n^2) and slow for large lists; generate neighbours instead.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ cities.length ≤ 10^5 (not stated in the source)
  • Each city, startCity and endCity is exactly three lowercase English letters.
  • startCity and endCity appear in cities.
